note: Work: the Employment Act, 2000 (No. 6 of 2000), section 21(1): no person under fourteen may be employed or work in any public or private agricultural, industrial or non-industrial undertaking, save work in homes and in vocational schools or training institutions (section 21(2)); section 22 bars 14 to 18 from harmful work. The Act makes no exception for performers, so the form holds them barred below fourteen (my reading). Read from the Ministry of Labour's copy. Majority: held as eighteen from the Constitution as amended by the Constitution (Amendment) (No. 3) Act, 2017 (No. 15 of 2017), s. 23(6): a child is a person under eighteen; a reading, as Myanmar's is, since no statute naming an age of majority was found. Read 2026-11-03 in the Constitute Project's text of the Constitution with amendments through 2017; the Act's own copy (malawilaws.com) answered 500 and MalawiLII 403. The Government portal's copy (malawi.gov.mw), read 2026-10-31, is the text before the 2017 amendment and sets marriage at 15 to 18 with consent, not majority. Service: no conscription law was found and the Malawi Defence Force's pages weren't read; left null. Until 2026-11-03 the majority stood null, no statute on it found (MalawiLII and Parliament's site put this client behind a Cloudflare check).
